public_rationale: On July 22, 2025, OpenAI reported that parts of Abilene were operating and running early workloads, while describing additional Oracle capacity separately [e1]. In its September 10, 2026 earnings discussion, Oracle reported delivering 131,000 GPUs at Abilene during fiscal Q1, June 1–August 31, 2026 [e2]. The earlier operations challenge a broad assertion that no Oracle–OpenAI capacity existed [e1]. But these disclosures do not establish that the disputed capacity existed before the post, verify substantive delivery and payment under the specific agreement, or establish its definitive termination without performance [e1] [e2]. Neither component is settled by this evidence [e1] [e2].
limitations: The July 2025 disclosure distinguishes Abilene from the additional Oracle capacity; it does not establish that Abilene performed the disputed agreement [e1].
Oracle's reported deliveries do not verify payment under that agreement [e2].
The June–August 2026 delivery total does not identify how much was delivered before the July 15, 2026 post [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The OpenAI-driven Oracle compute deal behind Oracle's RPO will never happen; the capacity never existed.

statement.excerpt: The capacity never existed, this deal will never happen, and you all know it and are either hopelessly ignorant or craven beyond words.

our_interpretation: The main forecast concerns performance of the Oracle–OpenAI compute agreement identified in the context, not merely signing an agreement.
Actual delivery and paid use attributable to that agreement would refute the ordinary meaning of 'will never happen'; completion of every promised facility is not required.
The historical capacity assertion concerns capacity associated with that agreement before the post. Capacity under a separate or earlier agreement cannot automatically settle it.
The surrounding text supplies a $300 billion contract figure but does not identify its accounting or reporting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Definitive termination or extinguishment of the identified agreement without substantive delivery or paid use, together with records establishing that its promised capacity had not existed before the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented delivery and payment for compute under the identified agreement, or direct evidence that the capacity denied by the historical assertion already existed.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Meanwhile, construction of Stargate I'
evidence.explanation: This challenges a broad reading that no Oracle–OpenAI capacity existed. It does not establish that Abilene constituted performance of the particular additional-capacity agreement.
Management reports substantial Abilene delivery during fiscal Q1. Delivery at this site does not by itself establish the contract attribution and payment required by the resolution rule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Records identifying the disputed agreement and verifying substantive delivery and payment under it would contradict the forecast. Records tying operational capacity before the post to that agreement would settle the historical assertion against the claim. Supporting both components requires definitive extinguishment without substantive delivery or paid use, plus records establishing that the promised capacity had not existed before the post.
